sections.heading: Softening a command
sections.body:
A bare imperative can sound abrupt. Soften it with:

- *por favor* and a diminutive: *Espérame un momentito, por favor.*
- a question: *¿Me pasas la sal?* (present) / *¿Me pasarías la sal?* (conditional — politer) / *¿Podrías cerrar la ventana?*
- *¿Te importa si…?* / *¿Le molestaría…?* (Would you mind…?)
- *si no es mucha molestia* (if it's not too much trouble)

In much of Latin America, requests with the plain imperative are softened by tone and *¿sí?*: *Pásame la sal, ¿sí?*

sections.heading: Strengthening a command
sections.body: *¡Que te calles!* (I said be quiet!) — *que* + subjunctive repeats or insists on an order. *¡Te dije que vinieras!* *¡Ni se te ocurra!* (Don't even think about it!) *¡Ya!* (Now! / Enough!) *¡Fuera de aquí!* (Get out of here!)

sections.heading: Que + subjunctive wishes
sections.body: *Que* + subjunctive expresses wishes to someone: *¡Que te vaya bien!* (Hope it goes well!) *¡Que tengas buen viaje!* *¡Que te mejores!* (Get well soon!) *¡Que lo pases bien!* (Have fun!) *¡Que descanses!* (Rest well!) *¡Que cumplas muchos más!* (Many happy returns!)

sections.heading: Imperatives as set phrases
sections.body: Some imperatives have become interjections: *¡Anda!* (Wow! / Go on!), *¡Vamos!* (Come on!), *¡Dale!* (OK! / Go for it! — Southern Cone, Caribbean, very common), *¡Órale!* (Mexico — OK / come on / wow), *¡Mira!* (Look! / Well…), *¡Oye!* (Hey!), *¡Fíjate!* (Imagine that! / Look at this!), *¡Dime!* (Tell me / Yes? — answering). *Venga* is mainly Spain.

examples: Wait for me a moment, please.
Can you pass me the salt?
Would you pass me the salt?
Do you mind if I open the window?
Si no es mucha molestia, ¿me ayuda con esto?
If it's not too much trouble, could you help me with this?
Pass me the salt, will you?
Shall we go to the movies? — OK!
Imagine that! She won the lottery.
